Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Africa | National Language barriers, import duties hindering Africa’s trade potential – Sierra Leone Mayor Source : Albert Kuzor 25 November 2026 3:13pm Yvonne Aki-Sawyerr in an interview with JoyBusiness at the Summit ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
The mayor of Freetown in Sierra Leone, Yvonne Aki-Sawyerr, says language differences, import duties and divergent policies among African countries continue to hinder the continent's ability to fully harness its trade potential.
She says despite Africa's growing population and huge market opportunities, persistent barriers between countries make it difficult for businesses to expand and trade across borders.
In an interview with JoyBusiness on the sidelines of the 6th German-African Business Summit (GABS) 2026 in Accra, she said African countries must address these challenges to strengthen economic integration and unlock the continent's opportunities.
“The strength of Africa really is in the fact that our population is young and our population is growing and it's actually a huge market. But it's a market that's not being fully tapped, not in any way, because of all of the barriers between us,” she said.
Ms Aki-Sawyerr cited the challenges businesses face when trading between neighbouring countries, including Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire, where language differences, import duties and varying policies can complicate commercial activities.
“So, you know, between Ghana and Cote d'Ivoire, your neighbours, but the language is a barrier. Import duties, different policies, the lack of harmonisation,” she said.
She called for stronger regional cooperation and the removal of barriers that prevent African businesses from accessing markets within the continent, arguing that greater integration could help businesses take advantage of Africa's sizeable market.
The Mayor of Freetown was speaking after participating in a panel discussion titled “New African-German Partnerships: Are the Rules Fit for Purpose?” at the summit, which is exploring ways to deepen economic relations between Germany and Africa.
